About the Olympiad

An Olympic format for environmental learning

The Sustainable Olympiad uses an Olympic competition format to teach environmental issues. Students test their knowledge about sustainability and the environment, solve challenges using creativity, and earn certificates that open doors to future opportunities.

  • Test your knowledge

    About sustainability and the environment.

  • Solve challenges

    Using knowledge and creativity.

  • Earn certificates

    That open doors to future opportunities.

SDG 4

Quality Education

The Sustainable Olympiad is aligned with SDG 4: inclusive, equitable and quality education for everyone.

PORTO talks logo

A PORTO talks project: “The world as seen by the students”

Our objectives

What the Olympiad sets out to do

  • Increase environmental knowledge among students

  • Improve science education and student engagement

  • Encourage genuine interest in sustainability

  • Identify and develop new talents

  • Create opportunities through certificates

  • Promote sustainability and environmental skills

Who can participate

Four levels

Students compete in the level that matches their school year.

  1. Level

    1

    5th and 6th grade

  2. Level

    2

    7th and 8th grade

  3. Level

    3

    9th grade and 1st year of High School

  4. Level

    4

    2nd and 3rd year of High School

How it works

Three phases

Every level goes through the same three phases, in order.

  1. 1

    Phase 1

    Test

    Questions about sustainability and the environment.

  2. 2

    Phase 2

    Riddle

    Solve an environmental riddle using knowledge and creativity.

  3. 3

    Phase 3

    Final Test

    A final test to complete the competition.

Certificates

Your effort counts

Participants receive certificates that can be used for future opportunities.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Who can participate?

Students from 5th grade to the 3rd year of High School, in four levels:

  • Level 1: 5th and 6th grade
  • Level 2: 7th and 8th grade
  • Level 3: 9th grade and 1st year of High School
  • Level 4: 2nd and 3rd year of High School
How many phases are there?

There are three phases:

  • Phase 1 – Test: questions about sustainability and the environment.
  • Phase 2 – Riddle: solve an environmental riddle using knowledge and creativity.
  • Phase 3 – Final Test: a final test to complete the competition.
Do participants get a certificate?

Yes. Participants receive certificates that can be used for future opportunities.
